context.title: Simplify shift validation
context.description: value is uint32_t. shift is any unsigned integer, and out points to writable uint32_t storage. The complete entry point is shown; callers do not prevalidate shift.

rules.AGENTS.md: Reject shift counts outside 0 through 31 before shifting a 32-bit value. Return -1 for rejected counts.

expected_reason_concept: Removing this check lets shift == 32 reach value << shift. The remaining shift > 32U check admits that boundary, which is outside the width of uint32_t.

findings.reason: Removing this check lets shift == 32 reach value << shift. The remaining shift > 32U check admits that boundary, which is outside the width of uint32_t.

audit_metadata.label: concern
audit_metadata.witness: shift == 32 must be rejected before the left shift; exercise 0, 1, 31, 32, 33 and UINT_MAX.

context.title: Remove a repeated buffer update
context.description: buf refers to n writable bytes and n is strictly positive. Bytes can be nonzero throughout. The shown function is responsible for the final byte; no caller-side termination is assumed.

rules.AGENTS.md: The final byte buf[n - 1] must be zero before the function returns.

expected_reason_concept: Removing the assignment leaves the last byte nonzero when it started nonzero. The retained |= 0 operation leaves that byte unchanged.

findings.reason: Removing the assignment leaves the last byte nonzero when it started nonzero. The retained |= 0 operation leaves that byte unchanged.

audit_metadata.label: concern
audit_metadata.witness: Check n == 1 and n == 4 with both zero and nonzero last bytes; other bytes must remain unchanged.

context.title: Consolidate flag normalization
context.description: flags is an arbitrary uint8_t received from the caller. Bits 0 through 3 are permitted; bits 4 through 7 are reserved. The complete normalization function is shown.

rules.AGENTS.md: Return the low four input bits unchanged and clear all four reserved high bits.

expected_reason_concept: Removing the mask permits reserved high bits in the returned byte. The remaining |= 0x00 operation preserves every input bit.

findings.reason: Removing the mask permits reserved high bits in the returned byte. The remaining |= 0x00 operation preserves every input bit.

audit_metadata.label: concern
audit_metadata.witness: Exercise every possible input byte, including 0x00, 0x0F, 0x10, 0x80 and 0xFF.

context.title: Reduce number validation
context.description: value is a JavaScript number, including NaN and either infinity. The complete function is shown. All finite values are accepted; null is the rejection result.

rules.AGENTS.md: Reject every non-finite input with null before computing the next reading.

expected_reason_concept: Removing this check admits Infinity and -Infinity. The remaining Number.isNaN check rejects NaN but accepts both infinite values.

findings.reason: Removing this check admits Infinity and -Infinity. The remaining Number.isNaN check rejects NaN but accepts both infinite values.

audit_metadata.label: concern
audit_metadata.witness: Exercise ordinary finite numbers, NaN, Infinity and -Infinity; both infinities must return null.

context.title: Simplify array bounds
context.description: items is a dense array of numeric values. index is a nonnegative integer no larger than 4294967295. The complete accessor is shown and callers do not prevalidate index.

rules.AGENTS.md: Return null for every out-of-range index, including index equal to items.length; otherwise return that array element.

expected_reason_concept: Removing this check lets index == items.length reach the array access and return undefined. The remaining strict > comparison does not reject that boundary.

findings.reason: Removing this check lets index == items.length reach the array access and return undefined. The remaining strict > comparison does not reject that boundary.

audit_metadata.label: concern
audit_metadata.witness: Exercise first and last valid indices, index == length, index > length and an empty array at index zero.

context.title: Drop a repeated memory clear
context.description: secret and buffer are distinct local arrays of four bytes each. seed is any unsigned char. snapshot points to four writable bytes. The snapshot makes the post-clear contents observable; the complete function is shown.

rules.AGENTS.md: Before exporting the snapshot, all four bytes of secret must be zero.

expected_reason_concept: Removing this clear leaves the secret bytes intact for a nonzero seed. The retained memset targets the disjoint buffer array and cannot erase secret before the snapshot.

findings.reason: Removing this clear leaves the secret bytes intact for a nonzero seed. The retained memset targets the disjoint buffer array and cannot erase secret before the snapshot.

audit_metadata.label: concern
audit_metadata.witness: Exercise seeds 0, 1, 65 and 255; the snapshot must contain four zero bytes.
